name: Thabit ibn Aslam al-Bunani
nameAr: ثابت بن أسلم البناني، أبو محمد، البصري

orthography.spelled: al-Bunani, with dammah on the ba' and two light nuns

diedNote: “twenty-odd” after 100 AH, aged 86 (Taqrib); 122, 123, 126, 127 and 129 are given (Shamela record)

teachers.name: Anas ibn Malik
teachers.source: Sahih al-Bukhari 4663; Ibn Hibban: he kept Anas's company for forty years

students.name: Ja'far ibn Sulayman al-Duba'i
students.source: Ibn Shahin, al-Afrad, as cited in Fath al-Bari on 3653

students.name: Hammad ibn Zayd
students.source: Sahih al-Bukhari 200 (Hammad ibn Zayd, from Thabit, from Anas)

verdicts.en: Asked whether Thabit or Qatadah is firmer: Thabit is careful in hadith.

verdicts.ar: أثبت أصحاب أنس الزهري، ثم ثابت، ثم قتادة
verdicts.en: The firmest of Anas's students is al-Zuhri, then Thabit, then Qatadah.

verdicts.ar: كان من أعبد أهل البصرة، وصحب أنسا أربعين سنة
verdicts.en: He was among the most devout of the people of Basra, and kept Anas's company for forty years.
verdicts.source: al-Thiqat, as quoted in Ikmal Tahdhib al-Kamal 3/63

dhahabi.en: He was a leader in knowledge and in practice.
dhahabi.source: al-Kashif, as given on the Shamela record

flags.label: Named only “Thabit” in hadith 4663
flags.detail: Other Successors named Thabit narrate from Anas, but the Basran who narrates from Anas to Hammam and whom Abu Hatim ranks second among Anas's students is al-Bunani, Anas's companion of forty years.

bio: The Basran ascetic who sat with Anas for forty years and became, after al-Zuhri, the most trusted channel of his hadith. He is one of the four consecutive Basrans in the cave hadith, and the only link in it from whom the report's single transmitter, Hammam, took it.
